name: Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Spallation Neutron Source
notes: Release pass 2 (2026-10-25): the linac structure and the Instrument Hall were placed by georeferencing ORNL's own interactive map ('Chestnut Ridge', labelled building polygons without coordinates) onto OpenStreetMap footprints; both are approximate and the method, its residuals and its limits are in the records and in docs/atlas-worklog/RELEASE_GEOMETRY_accel2.md.

COHERENT's four operating sub-detectors (CENNS-10, CsI, Ge, NaI) all sit in Neutrino Alley, officially 'about 20 meters from the SNS target' at its closest point and 50 m long overall (src:geo-ornl-neutrino-alley-qa); none is drawn individually, since no source gives any one detector's position along the alley or a coordinate/heading for the alley itself, only its overall length and closest-approach distance.

summary.plain: The Spallation Neutron Source at Oak Ridge National Laboratory, Tennessee: the long linac building and the instrument hall that holds the mercury target are drawn at true scale inside the complex boundary. The accumulator ring and the two beam-transport lines are underground and have no published position, so they are listed as not located.
summary.technical: One local map for facility:oak-ridge-national-laboratory. Drawn: the OSM footprint of the linac structure (front-end building, klystron gallery and tunnel; 370 m, accelerator:sns) and of the Instrument Hall (building 8700), both identified by georeferencing the polygons of ORNL's interactive map, plus the Guest House and 22 other OSM buildings. Not located: the 248 m accumulator ring, the HEBT (169 m), the RTBT (151 m), the target's position inside building 8700 and Neutrino Alley.

unlocated.backlog: A published SNS site or tunnel layout with a scale bar, coordinates or surveyed control points (the 1999 SNS EIS site plan, a civil-construction drawing set, or an IWAA/PAC survey paper giving ring-centre and linac-axis coordinates); georeference it against the linac structure and the 8700 hall drawn here (cite, never copy), then add length checks against 248.0 m (ring), 169 m (HEBT) and 151 m (RTBT). Do not draw the ring as a circle: it is a four-arc, four-straight-section lattice, and the layout figure in PAC 2003 TPPE011 is an unscaled schematic.
unlocated.reason: SNS accumulator ring (circumference 248.0 m), High Energy Beam Transport (169 m) and Ring-to-Target Beam Transport (151 m) lines. They are buried under the earth berm and are not mapped in OpenStreetMap (the complex holds only 25 building footprints, none of them a ring); ORNL's interactive map draws only the linac gallery, the Instrument Hall, CLO, CNMS, JINS and the Guest House; and the only layout figure found (PAC 2003 TPPE011, Fig. 1) is a labelled schematic without scale, coordinates or north. The derived distance from the linac end to the 8700 hall (about 220 m in this map) would not fix the ring's position, and the ring is a four-superperiod lattice, so no circle is drawn. The atlas has no accelerator record for the ring or the transfer lines (accelerator:sns is drawn through the linac structure).

unlocated.backlog: A COHERENT or SNS paper with a plan view of the target building basement and the alley (a scaled drawing or measured offsets from the target to each detector), or a basement drawing from ORNL; then place it from the 8700 footprint.
unlocated.reason: Neutrino Alley (the COHERENT detector corridor) and the target position. ORNL says the corridor is 50 m long and 'about 20 meters from the SNS target' at its closest point, and ORNL's map says the Instrument Hall (8700) 'contains the SNS back-end system including the heavy-metal target'; but no fetched source gives the target's position inside the 8700 footprint, the alley's bearing, or which building lies above it. The site is accounted for on the map by the complex boundary (drawn); the corridor and the COHERENT detectors are not drawn.
